newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thousands ring Thai premier's office.
newsitem.headline: Thousands ring Thai premier's office.

text.p: Thousands of noisy and frustrated Thai protesters on Tuesday ringed Government House where the prime minister's office is located and blocked most exits from the building, police said.
But they later made way for Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh to leave his office.
The estimated 15,000 villagers, who came to the capital in late January from impoverished northeast Thailand to demand social justice, have camped around the building since then.
After making way for the prime minister, the protesters moved away from the Government House gates and went back to their makeshift camps some distance away from the building.
A government official said earlier the mob had blocked most exits from Government House and refused to leave until the prime minister came to meet them and discussed their demands.
Chavalit told reporters before leaving Government House that he recognised the villagers had problems that needed to be solved.
"We have to heed their demands and appreciate their hardships, but sometimes things cannot be done quickly and they should understand this," he said.
About 300 anti-riot police were on alert at the scene, but they did not need to take action, witnesses said.
Spokesmen for the protesters told Reuters they were dissatisfied with a lack of progress in their negotiations with the government on settling their demands since late-January.
The protesters, organised by a movement called the Assembly of the Poor, want to be freed from debt owed to the state-owned Agriculture and Cooperatives Bank.
They also seek higher prices for their produce and settlement of their land disputes with the government.
The group has lived in makeshift tents, cooking their food and bathing on the street in the scorching heat.
